name: Real Estate
one_liner: Real estate owners, developers and service firms create value from land and buildings, with economics driven by rents, occupancy, financing costs and property values.
how_it_makes_money: Owners and REITs earn rental income and capture appreciation when values rise; developers profit from building or repositioning assets and selling or leasing them up. Service firms such as brokers and property managers earn commissions and fees on transactions and managed space.
revenue_formula: Rental revenue = rentable square feet (or units) × occupancy × average rent
Net operating income (NOI) = rental and other revenue - property operating expenses
cost_structure: Interest expense: financing costs, highly sensitive to rates
Property operating expenses: maintenance, utilities, staffing
Property taxes and insurance: rising insurance costs in climate-exposed markets
Capital expenditures: tenant improvements, leasing commissions, renovations
Development costs: land, construction and soft costs for developers
margins: Stabilized properties typically convert a large share of revenue to NOI, and returns depend heavily on leverage, entry cap rate and rent growth; the spread across sectors reflects demand for each property type.

key_metrics.name: Net operating income (NOI)
key_metrics.what: Property income after operating costs but before financing; the basis for valuation.

key_metrics.name: Capitalization rate (cap rate)
key_metrics.what: NOI divided by property value; the market's required yield, moving with interest rates.

key_metrics.name: Occupancy rate
key_metrics.what: Share of space leased; drives revenue and signals demand.

key_metrics.name: Funds from operations (FFO)
key_metrics.what: REIT earnings adding back depreciation; the standard REIT profitability measure.

key_metrics.name: Loan-to-value (LTV)
key_metrics.what: Debt relative to property value; measures leverage and refinancing risk.

key_metrics.name: Weighted average lease term (WALT)
key_metrics.what: Remaining lease duration; indicates income stability.

key_metrics.name: Same-store NOI growth
key_metrics.what: NOI growth for properties owned in both periods; shows organic performance.

trends: Office distress from hybrid work, with a gap between prime and older buildings
Higher interest rates pressuring valuations and triggering refinancing challenges
Strong demand for data centers driven by AI and cloud growth
Housing affordability and supply shortages shaping residential and build-to-rent
Office-to-residential conversions being explored in many cities
Rising insurance costs and climate risk affecting property economics
